summary.text: A mid-ocean ridge is an underwater mountain system that forms along a divergent plate boundary, where the seafloor spreads apart.
As the plates separate, mantle rises and melts, and the magma erupts as lava that cools into new oceanic crust.
Most ridges are connected in one global system that is part of every ocean, making it the longest mountain range in the world.

items.prompt: Where is the longest mountain range on Earth?

options.label: Along the west side of South America
On the ocean floor, linking every ocean

items.explain: Most mid-ocean ridges are connected into one global system that is part of every ocean, making it the longest mountain range in the world, several times longer than the Andes.

items.prompt: A ship drills seafloor rock samples along a line heading away from a ridge's central axis. What pattern in the rocks' ages does it find?

options.label: They get younger farther from the axis
They get older farther from the axis
They are all the same age

items.explain: New crust forms at the axis, so the rocks are youngest there and grow older with distance from it.

items.prompt: Seafloor far from a ridge sits deeper than seafloor near it. Why?

options.label: Sediment piling on top pushes it down
As it cools, the material beneath grows denser

items.explain: Away from the ridge the plate cools and its mantle lithosphere thickens and becomes denser, so older seafloor sits deeper.

items.prompt: Roughly how fast do the plates move apart at mid-ocean ridges?
items.explain: Spreading rates range from about 10 to 200 mm per year.

items.prompt: How can scientists work out how fast a ridge has been spreading?

options.label: By timing how long fresh lava takes to cool
By counting earthquakes along the ridge each year
By measuring how warm the seawater is above it
By mapping magnetic patterns locked into the crust

items.explain: Cooling basalt records the direction of Earth's magnetic field, which has flipped at known intervals, so the pattern gives the crust's age and, with distance from the axis, the spreading rate.

items.prompt: One ridge widens by about 25 mm each year, another by about 120 mm each year. Which would you expect to have a large rift valley along its crest?
items.explain: Ridges spreading slower than 40 mm a year generally have large rift valleys, while those faster than 90 mm a year lack them.
